speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The Ministry of Law (MinLaw) has strategically built and strengthened Singapore's reputation as a legal hub.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In so doing, several excellent initiatives have been launched: the physical expansion of Maxwell Chambers, thereby further boosting the Singapore International Arbitration Centre's (SIAC's) reputation as an exceptional arbitral education centre; the Singapore International Mediation Centre (SIMC) and the Singapore International Commercial Court (SICC).

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: By providing these platforms, Singapore provides a complete suite of dispute resolution mechanisms alongside the Singapore Courts.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I should declare my interest as a member of the Singapore Bar who practises both courtroom and arbitral litigation.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Within the practice of law, Singapore's reputation for being a legal hub has been further established through local firms with cross-border expertise; through international firms situated in Singapore, through the qualified foreign law practice (QFLP) route, and through local firms entering into joint law ventures (JLVs) with international firms.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Our local firms lean on the international networks of the London or New York-based firms, while the London and New York firms lean on the Singapore firms' clear, relevant and up-to-date knowledge and expertise of Singapore law, as well as the Singapore firms' knowledge of the region.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: With regard to dispute resolution in particular, Singapore's reputation as a choice arbitration centre is testament to the excellent growth of the adjudication mechanism of arbitration and the service provided by SIAC.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Singapore's proximity, neutrality, reputation for rule of law and efficiency have been able to attract parties from all over the world, not just the region, but the world ‒ from India, China, South Korea, Australia, Vietnam, the US, Hong Kong, Indonesia, British Virgin Islands and Malaysia ‒ to adjudicate here.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: To capture the increase in opportunities expected as regional demand for dispute resolution continues to grow, the expansion of Maxwell Chambers is timely.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The investment into expanding Maxwell Chambers reflects both MinLaw's commitment to strengthening Singapore's status as a legal hub, as well as SIAC's high service standards, which I have personally encountered and experienced.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It reflects both the long-term trajectory and the present quality of SIAC and MinLaw.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In my opinion, the epitome of a legal hub is being the choice jurisdiction in which companies and individuals choose to have their rights adjudicated and arbitrated.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: How much better for Singapore's reputation as a rule-of-law society and country if the companies and individuals choose Singapore law as the governing law of the dispute?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This will allow Singapore law to be developed and its jurisprudence, where valid and worthy, to be exported.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It will also be a good advertisement for Singapore, that is, our laws work and can be applied well within the context of global and regional commerce.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: What is key for this to happen is the use of Singapore law as the governing law in dispute resolution clauses in both Singapore, Singapore party contracts, as well as Singapore foreign-party contracts.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If the Ministry views the increased use of Singapore law at home and abroad as a positive development, what plans does MinLaw have to further strengthen Singapore's status as a dispute resolution hub, and how does it plan to promote Singapore law within that push?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If I may, Mdm Chair, my next cut?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Access to justice is important in every rule-of-law society, every rule-of-law country.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Initiatives, such as the Criminal Legal Aid Scheme (CLAS) and Legal Assistance for Capital Offences (LASCO), serve this important function in our criminal justice system.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Last year, through the support of MinLaw, CLAS was able to employ two more senior advocates to mentor the other lawyers and to take on high-stake cases.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Would the Minister provide an update on what further can be done to ensure access to justice for accused persons who may not necessarily be able to afford counsel?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: In terms of civil justice ‒ for there is criminal justice and then there is also civil justice ‒ in terms of civil justice, event-triggered fee arrangements have been debated but not without some controversy to promote access to justice.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Would the Minister provide an update on the review to event-triggered fee arrangements in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Second Schedule of the Legal Aid and Advice Act sets out the requirements that have to be satisfied for the grant of legal aid.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There is some form of discretion given to the Director of Legal Aid but there are conditions attached to the exercise of these decisions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As a result, some truly deserving cases fall through the crack and legal aid is not granted.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Will the Minister consider an amendment to the Act to allow for appeals to the Minister, for legal aid for such cases provided that the Director grants leave for such an appeal?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In 2016, we saw significant positive changes in Singapore's legal industry arising from moves spearheaded by MinLaw.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: These are important steps to diversify and add depth to the legal industry and to support our push to be Asia's leading disputes resolution hub.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In our push to be the leading legal commercial hub, we must continue to upgrade services to those who require bread-and-butter justice.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: We must continue to ensure that justice is accessible and available to individuals when they need it.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: One such area is in non-contentious probate and administration matters.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Currently, when a loved one has passed away leaving behind a property, an administrator or executor will have to be appointed by the Court to administer the estate.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The administrator or executor will usually be a family member of the deceased.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: However, before the family member is legally recognised as an executor or administrator, he would first have to apply to Court for a Grant of Probate or Letter of Administration.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This process involves the Courts and involves engaging lawyers and may be time-consuming.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In our push towards digitisation and the greater use of data analytics, we should think about how to best harness the benefits of the digital age to improve our community services.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Perhaps, a good comparison could be the Silver Support Scheme which is automatically extended to Singaporeans aged 65 and above who meet certain criteria.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Perhaps, the Ministry could consider looking into how we may similarly use available personal information to shorten or simplify the procedure of obtaining a grant in non-contentious probate and administration cases.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng, you have two cuts.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: In my constituency work, I have met residents who found themselves on the wrong side of the law in either civil or criminal cases.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: They made a mistake, but the problem is compounded because they do not know how to navigate the legal system.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: In some cases, it happened upstream where my residents do not know whom to approach or where to seek guidance from, before signing a contract that may prove disadvantageous to them.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: What measures is MinLaw looking at to enhance access to justice and also to build basic legal awareness among the public?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Next, on legal hub, I would like to suggest the idea of "an academia of industry" ‒ a living ecosystem of cross-disciplinary deep skills and expertise; deep industry skills and knowledge to complement our internationally recognised law schools.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Imagine having more legal firms with in-house expertise in FinTech, Blockchain and even the evolving impact of Blockchain-mediated "smart contracts".

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Imagine legal teams with deep knowledge of biotech and the legal issues surrounding genomics or personalised medicine that straddle multiple jurisdictions.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Combining expertise across subject domains, this creates value and competitive advantage.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: And this can help us to provide skills and services in Singapore which no other legal hub can do.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Much has been said about the uncertain future economy.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The legal services sector will also need to respond to the changes in the economy and transform.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The developments in the region and Singapore's reputation in international commercial dispute resolution put it in good stead to find opportunities for local law practices.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The small and medium-sized law practices, may, however, find it challenging to compete at this level, especially if they have not been involved in any international practice.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: During the last Committee of Supply (COS) debate, the Ministry indicated that it was working with the Law Society more specifically to identify how to strengthen small and medium-sized law firms.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There are many different sectors within the legal industry.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: It would be useful for Singapore law practices to be guided on the emerging needs and trends of the legal industry in the future economy.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: What steps will the Ministry take to ensure continued growth and development of the different sectors within the industry?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Perhaps, there could be a holistic business consultancy service offered to the small and medium-sized law practices so that they can be made aware of emerging markets and the concrete steps to be part of those markets.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: My first cut is on the career pathway for in-house counseI.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I declare my interest as a corporate member of the Singapore Corporate Counsel Association (SCCA) and also a member of their Advisory Board.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Singapore should aim to be, and is certainly capable of becoming, the Asian hub for in-house legal capability.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: This will help attract multinational corporations (MNCs), whether Western or Asian, to invest or continue to invest, here.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: It will also feed the ambitions of SIAC, SIMC and SICC.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: In-house legal capability is highly exportable and it is not limited to the practice of Singapore law.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: To be truly regional, the capability should not be limited to Singapore law or English law.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: We should seek to build expertise in the laws of the various countries in the region.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Furthermore, the competencies of a regional legal counsel go beyond black letter law as they must encompass business management skills and ethical conduct.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: SCCA wants to encourage recruiters, employers and in-house counsel to use the framework as a reference guide to hiring, training and career development.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: The Competency Framework will be reviewed regularly to keep up to date with the market.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Singapore is one of the few countries in which in-house counsel are not required to meet any form of professional standards or any form of continuing education.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: This will come as a surprise to many a person in the boardroom, despite the fact that in-house legal advice privilege has been granted via statute.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: A mandatory Competency Framework will compel in-house counsel in Singapore to acquire baseline knowledge that is relevant to his or her role, which constitutes a form of quality assurance to all who set up regional legal functions in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: This will improve the quality of the legal talent pool in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Some quarters may say these mandatory standards and continuing education may translate into costs.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I submit that even the in-house community needs to embrace Continuing Education and Training (CET), deep-skilling and SkillsFuture to stay ready, relevant and resilient.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I have spoken on this before and am raising it again to the Minister.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I hope MinLaw will seriously look into reviewing the jurisdictional limits of the Small Claims Tribunal (SCT) so that more people can have economical and expedient orders and judgment to their contractual claims.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: In particular, I know many professional freelancers who are on a contract for service use SCT when they are not paid for their work rendered.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Raising the claim limits will be a boon to claimants and freelance workers alike.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Since coming in force in November 2014, can MinLaw provide an update on the number of cases filed and mediated?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Among all the Prevention of Harassment Act cases filed, what is the breakdown on the types, that is, how many involve community and neighbours, and how many are online, sexual and workplace harassment cases?

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Fundamentally, in the areas of law and justice, we rank well because of our strong societal and institutional foundations.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: With that as the background, let me now speak about the legal sector.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Like many other sectors, the legal sector faces some challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I will touch on what we are doing to make Singapore a leading legal hub and to support the legal industry.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: First, on strengthening our status as a dispute resolution hub.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Over the years, we have systematically built up our dispute resolution capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We are now among the top five most preferred seats of arbitration in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We have well-regarded institutions which offer a suite of top-quality dispute resolution services, such as SIAC, SIMC and SICC.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We are also continuing to grow dispute resolution activities in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We are renovating and refurbishing the Red Dot Traffic Building and expanding the premises of Maxwell Chambers.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: This will increase the capacity at Maxwell Chambers and we can have more hearings there.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It will also help attract more international institutions, arbitration chambers and law firms to do that kind of work in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Second, on the promotion and use of Singapore law.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Our legal sector can benefit from the promotion of Singapore in the region.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Today, we do see an increasing use of Singapore law in cross-border transactions in this region.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Singapore law is one of the default options in some Baltic and International Maritime Council standard forms.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Growth in this trend must come from businesses, led by parties and industries.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They will benefit from an emergence of a default Asian law.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: My Ministry has also financially supported the development of centres of excellence as an added factor specialising in a number of areas, including regional law.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: To name a few: the Centre for Asian Legal Studies, the Centre for Banking and Finance Law and the Centre for Law and Business.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: These institutions will help to grow Singapore's reputation as a thought leader in the law, anchor regional legal expertise in Singapore and strengthen the recognition and use of Singapore law.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Ms Rahayu asked if Singapore Law Practices (SLPs) could be made aware of emerging markets and the concrete steps SLPs can take to be part of those markets.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: There are a number of schemes available to assist SLPs in regionalisation, for example, Enterprise Singapore's (IE's) Global Company Partnership scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It provides support, including financial support, to Singapore law firms to build market expertise via secondments to other places.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: IE also has a Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It allows our law firms to deduct the expenses for overseas business development and investment study trips against taxable income.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: My Ministry will continue working with the relevant economic agencies to support SLPs in their growth plans and regionalisation efforts because we have to look outside Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We are also looking to establish ourselves as a centre for international debt restructuring in Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We are well-positioned to do that because we are a major financial, legal and business hub.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We have the expertise, efficiency and legal framework.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: My Ministry has, therefore, worked with the Ministry of Finance on the Companies (Amendment) Bill, and that will enhance Singapore's debt restructuring processes.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We are also working with parties from the public and private sectors to promote our debt restructuring regime, attract other influential players to base themselves in Singapore and develop multidisciplinary training and education for professionals in the industry.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Beyond dispute resolution and restructuring, we are looking to develop and grow new practice areas.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: More will be shared when the Committee on the Future Economy (CFE) Working Group on Legal and Accounting Services releases its report in April.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We will also continue to develop intellectual property (IP) as a growth area.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It is important that the IP regime allows businesses to develop and commercialise IP in a cost-effective way.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We are considering ways to improve our IP dispute resolution mechanism and we are considering the recommendations made by the IP Dispute Resolution Committee.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Ms Rahayu asked about the study my Ministry did with the Law Society to identify the technology and capability needs of small and medium SLPs.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The study identified technology adoption as a key area of development for SLPs.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The larger firms are able to invest in money, but I think the smaller firms have challenges in keeping up, making the investments, with rapidly-changing technological advancements.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We have worked with the Law Society and SPRING, and we have kick-started the adoption of technology by SLPs.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Earlier this week, we launched the "Tech Start for Law" programme.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: This will provide SLPs with support of up to 70% of the cost to adopt basic technology products for practice management, online legal research and online marketing.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We really hope that SLPs will take advantage of it.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: My Ministry will go out with the message as aggressively as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I have outlined some of the ways in which my Ministry is working to support the legal industry.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We will provide the necessary partnership, framework, support and incentives.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The legal profession and the private sector have to come into that partnership, embrace the changes, grasp the opportunities, some of which are disruptive.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They really have to keep up with the developments in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations and beyond and strive to understand the regional market and distinguish themselves by the quality of their work and their business acumen because a fair part of the law is becoming commoditised through technology.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Together we can ensure that our legal industry remains vibrant and competitive in the years ahead.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To ensure that our legal industry continues to be vibrant and competitive internationally, the key stakeholders of the industry must actively embrace disruptive changes and grasp the opportunities at hand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These include private practitioners, in-house counsel and law students.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Working Group report will be released next month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It contains several key recommendations to position the Singapore legal and accounting services sector for the future, in particular, the need to build thought leadership through driving standards and research and equipping legal professionals to be future-ready through deepening skillsets and industry expertise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: MinLaw will be working closely with the legal industry to achieve the outcomes envisaged in the recommendations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It took in its first cohort of 60 students in January 2017.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Eighty percent of the cohort are mature students with work and life experience and seeking a mid-career switch to law.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Their experience will stand them in good stead to deal with the emotional demands of family and criminal law.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The UniSIM law school curriculum is practice-oriented to better prepare the students for practice when they graduate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We also want to develop future-ready legal professionals who will be able to pursue the new opportunities that will arise in high-growth areas while leveraging new technology and innovation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng spoke about the need for our lawyers to possess cross-disciplinary skills and expertise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is important, especially in today's increasingly complex business environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To provide holistic advice, lawyers must have deep knowledge of their business and industries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This can be achieved through a more multidisciplinary and practice-oriented law curriculum, as well as targeted efforts in continuing professional development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, the UniSIM School of Law has a multidisciplinary curriculum where law students learn not only the law, but also have electives in social work, counselling, psychology, forensics and criminology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will get feedback from the industry on the skills needed by young lawyers, study international best practices in legal education, and work closely with the National University of Singapore (NUS), Singapore Management University (SMU) and UniSIM to update their law curriculum to better prepare our law graduates for the future economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Some of our law students have already taken the first step towards developing such multidisciplinary and practice-oriented skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, a common interest in legal technology and innovation led a group of NUS students to start a ground-up initiative, called "Alt+Law".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This initiative aspires to change the legal industry by exploring technological solutions for lawyers' tasks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This informal group, which includes Computer Science and Engineering students, hopes to use data analysis to supplement expert opinion for lawyers, policymakers and clients in areas, such as sentencing guidelines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These are the types of innovative and cross-disciplinary efforts that we must cultivate and encourage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There are also programmes on leadership and management, such as the Singapore Academy of Law (SAL)-INSEAD Law Firm Leadership Programme, as well as specialist knowledge in the identified growth areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Another significant group in the legal industry is the in-house counsel.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We note Mr Patrick Tay's suggestion to develop the talent pool of in-house counsel in Singapore and for a mandatory competency framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We agree that there should be continued efforts to develop the in-house sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have been working closely with the Economic Development Board to promote Singapore as a choice location for regional and global headquarters, including in-house counsel teams.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are actively encouraging companies to anchor their decision-makers with global or regional mandate in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We also encourage in-house counsel to continuously raise their standards of practice.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To this end, we will continue to work with the relevant stakeholders to make available programmes to help in-house counsel develop the appropriate skillsets and competencies to carry out their jobs well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: MinLaw will also monitor the progress and adoption of SCCA's competency framework with a view towards revisiting the issue of whether competency frameworks should be made mandatory in the future, taking into consideration the developments in the in-house counsel space.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Several Members filed cuts relating to enhancing access to justice.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The best laws and best Courts will be of little effect if the ordinary citizen has no access to them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: My Ministry is working closely with the Judiciary, the Law Society and other stakeholders to enhance access to justice, especially for the man-in-the-street, by ensuring legal aid and pro bono advice are available to those who need it and providing mechanisms to help resolve community disputes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Legal Aid Bureau provides civil legal aid to less-privileged Singaporeans who pass the means and merits test.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The means-test framework is regularly reviewed to allow persons of limited means to qualify for legal aid.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This translated into about 300,000 additional Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents who can potentially qualify for legal aid.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In response to Mr Louis Ng and Mr Murali Pillai's queries, the discretion to depart from the general means-test already exists for certain vulnerable groups of people, such as those who face hardship or are involved in certain family proceedings, to qualify for legal aid.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In 2007, we amended the means-test criteria to help persons facing hardship, such as sudden mental or physical disabilities, or the sudden loss of income.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In 2013, we amended the means-test criteria for persons in family proceedings involving children or protection orders, in order to protect the most vulnerable persons in family disputes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will continue to review and update the means-test framework and qualifying criteria to ensure access to justice for people who cannot afford to hire their own lawyer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This includes considering whether additional discretion should be granted to the Director of Legal Aid or other authority for exceptional cases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr de Souza asked specifically about legal aid for probate matters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, legal aid is available for such matters, if the applicant qualifies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Second, if the estate value does not exceed $50,000, the next-of-kin can also apply to the Public Trustee to administer the estate, subject to fulfilment of certain criteria.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Third, for estates exceeding $50,000, the next-of-kin may engage a lawyer to assist in the estate administration and the costs can be recovered from the estate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Criminal legal aid is available under the Criminal Legal Aid Scheme (CLAS) run by the Law Society's Pro Bono Services Office.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Since the launch of enhanced CLAS in 2015 and the Government started directly funding CLAS, the number of CLAS applicants has increased significantly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: More applicants are being helped because of the increased coverage of enhanced CLAS, such as under the Moneylenders Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, there was an elderly lady charged with assisting illegal moneylending because she was tricked into letting a stranger access her bank account.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: She was assigned a CLAS lawyer, who was ultimately able to get the charges dropped.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I am encouraged by the strong partnership and support from law firms for CLAS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Several law firms have taken on a significant number of CLAS cases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The largest five law firms in Singapore have also supported the CLAS Fellowship scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I hope law firms will continue to support CLAS and take on more cases on a regular basis to enhance access to justice.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Other than Government-funded legal aid, pro bono basic legal advice is also provided at many legal clinics across Singapore.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There are also family, civil and criminal legal clinics run at the State and Family Courts.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Law Society also has various schemes aimed at promoting legal awareness.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: These include general legal awareness talks, as well as the annual Law Awareness Week programmes.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: On community justice, we have put in place various mechanisms to resolve community disputes.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Our Community Mediation Centre has a good track record of mediating disputes in the community.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Disputes can also be resolved at the Community Disputes Resolution Tribunals (CDRT) and SCT.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Protection from Harassment Act (POHA) provides for simplified Court procedures and Court forms for Protection Order applications.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Tay spoke about initiatives in this area.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: These include the applications by victims of sexual, workplace and online harassment.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Out of the 46 applications referred to mediation at the State Courts Centre for Dispute Resolution, 23 were successfully settled and five are pending completion of mediation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There are different types of event-triggered fee arrangements and they have pros and cons.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In contingency fee arrangements, the lawyer shares in an agreed percentage of the sum recovered by the client where the claim is successful.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: On the one hand, there is certainty upfront as the lawyer's fees are directly tied to the amount the client recovers.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: On the other hand, the lawyer's fees have no correlation to the work done.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The lawyer could receive a large sum of money for a short trial, or a small sum for a protracted trial.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In conditional fee arrangements, the lawyer receives payment of his legal fees only if the claim is successful.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The arrangement may also allow for an uplift of fees in the event of success.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For such arrangements, the lawyer's fees are based on the amount of work done for the client.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But it also means that there is less certainty upfront about the fees that could be incurred.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There are also other considerations, for example, whether such arrangements would give rise to a potential conflict of interest, as the lawyer has a direct financial interest in the outcome of the litigation, and whether they may increase frivolous litigation or raise litigation costs.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We need to carefully assess these considerations to determine the framework which is most suitable for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: In my cut, I mentioned that the system basically has not changed and, even for non-contentious matters, the persons involved would have to make a Court application and involve lawyers as well.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I can say that we are actively reviewing not only that, but all other Court procedures where it is really for the community or the man-in-the-street.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: You will see that, in recent times, we have actually started simplifying various procedures.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: POHA, for example, is one such example where we try to make it such that the person does not need to actually instruct the lawyer in order to make an application.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, this is an area which we will study to see whether the procedures can be simplified.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: I just want to ask the Senior Minister of State, earlier on, on the POHA claims, since its inception in November 2014, how many of these that are filed involved harassment in workplaces?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I do not have a specific breakdown of the actual numbers for sexual and workplace harassment.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But if the Member wishes, perhaps, he can file a specific question on that.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Christopher de Souza, do you wish to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: SIAC, SIMC, SICC, third-party funding, these are excellent initiatives.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: They are the brainchild of MinLaw and collective innovative drives.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: These will further enhance and entrench Singapore's status as a legal hub.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: It leaves me, therefore, to thank MinLaw for its hard work and seek leave of the House to withdraw my amendment.
